overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: handwritten shorthand notes were not draft minutes, the whispered exchange was procedural and below quorum, and the lighting changes came from noticed subcommittee meetings. Subcommittee notice claims were outside its jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to provide May 8 meeting minutes within ten days of a request, arguing the clerk's handwritten notes were draft minutes.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the clerk's handwritten shorthand notes were not a draft of the May 8 meeting minutes the Committee was not obligated to provide them within ten days.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged two members privately deliberated by whispering during the May 8 meeting while the lighting policy vote was being taken.
allegations.key_passage: Not only were the comments of a procedural nature, but they did not reach a quorum of the Committee.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee deliberated outside a noticed meeting on field lighting policy, citing differences between proposals at two meetings.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee stated to our office that the changes at issue stemmed from the subcommittee meetings that took place on April 9 and 26.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the lighting subcommittee's meeting notices were insufficiently specific; the AG declined to review because only the committee was the complained-against body.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we cannot investigate allegations concerning other bodies.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
